full_judgment: 18. In the case of Dominion of India Vs. RB Sohan Lal, reported in AIR 1950 (East Punjab) 40, a similar matter came for decision before a Division Bench presided over by Das, CJ. In that case the Railway Administration by granting a licence gave the petitioner an exclusive right to sell newspapers, books, etc. and to erect book stalls on the station premises to expire after 5 years unless renewed. Clause 2 of the Agreement provided for termination of the contract for misconduct of the licensee. In a suit by the licensee for injunction restraining the Railway from terminating the contract, an ad interim injunction was granted which was taken on appeal before the High Court Division, East Punjab. The said was set aside by the High Court holding that the agreement is a mere revocable licence and an ad-interim injunction should not have been granted in this sort of matter. This Division Bench of the East Punjab High Court after discussing in detail a number of cases of English jurisdiction and of Indian Jurisdiction found that section 60 of the Indian Easements Act provided that licence may be revoked by the Manager unless it is coupled with the Transfer of Property and such transfer is in force or the licensee acting upon the licence has executed a work of a permanent character and incurs expenses in the execution, held that in order for a grant to be irrevocable, the licence had to be coupled with the transfer of property and not merely an interest as under the English Cases in the nature of profit and further the provision of the Indian Easements Act will give way to the special agreement if any of the parties. Thus although a licence under section 60 of the Easement Act may be irrevocable either because it is coupled with a grant or interest or because the licensee has created works of a permanent nature yet, there is nothing to prevent the parties from agreeing expressly or by necessary implication that the licence shall be revocable and on the same way there will be nothing to prevent the parties from agreeing expressly or impliedly that the licence which is prima facie revocable would be to irrevocable.
